bugs: A guest request to /api/me without an `Accept: application/json` header (for example a plain `GET` or `PATCH` from curl or a browser) returns 500, because the Authenticate middleware redirects to the undefined `route('login')`. The app never configures `redirectGuestsTo` (bootstrap/app.php unchanged). The guest test only covers JSON requests (tests/Feature/MeTest.php:6-8), so it misses this case.
antipatterns: app/Http/Resources/MeResource.php:14 — a dedicated JsonResource with `$wrap = null` for a three-field payload. It is idiomatic but adds a little ceremony; `$user->only()` would do the same job.
routes/api.php:11-12 — `prefix('me')` with `'/'` routes is less direct than declaring `/me` on each route.
app/Http/Requests/UpdateProfileRequest.php — the class is named UpdateProfileRequest while the controller and resource use Me naming.
strengths: The FormRequest uses `present|nullable|string|max:30`. Clearing works with null or an empty string, and leaving the field out returns 422.
The migration adds `string('nickname', 30)->nullable()->after('name')` and has a working `down()`.
The controller is thin: `update($request->validated())` writes only the validated field, so mass assignment is safe.

The tests are compact Pest tests that use datasets for the guest checks, the clear cases and the invalid cases. They check that the stored value is unchanged after a 422, check the 30-character boundary, ignore other fields, and confirm another user is not affected.

antipatterns: app/Http/Controllers/MeController.php:24-27 — the private `profile()` helper builds `response()->json($user->only(...))` by hand. That fits this size, but an API Resource would be the conventional choice if the payload grows.
tests/Feature/MeTest.php:56-84 — the separate validation-failure tests could be one dataset, as impl-1 does.
strengths: bootstrap/app.php adds `redirectGuestsTo(fn ($r) => $r->is('api/*') ? null : route('login'))`, so a non-JSON guest request to the API returns 401 instead of 500. A test covers this (MeTest.php:23).
The FormRequest has the same `present|nullable|string|max:30` rules, and the migration matches the requirement exactly.
The response is shaped with `$user->only(['id','name','nickname'])`, which is minimal and proportionate.

The tests are thorough. Both GET and PATCH use exact JSON assertions. They cover set, clear with null or an empty string, the 30 and 31 character boundaries, a non-string value, a missing field, extra name/email fields being ignored, and isolation from other users.

v.rationale: The two implementations are almost the same. Both have the same migration, `present|nullable|string|max:30` FormRequest, `validated()` update, Fillable change and test coverage, and all their tests pass (15 in impl-1, 14 in impl-2). My probes showed that both handle multibyte length, whitespace trimming to null, integer rejection and form-encoded PATCH correctly. The deciding difference is how they treat guests: a non-JSON guest request (no Accept header) returns 500 in impl-1, because the middleware redirects to an undefined `login` route. impl-2 configures `redirectGuestsTo` so API guests get 401 and adds a test for it. impl-1's API Resource is a reasonable idiom, but it does not outweigh that robustness gap. impl-2 is also slightly leaner.
